pause.title: Pause plan
pause.entryHint: Illness, injury or holiday – resume when you are ready.
pause.rules: When you resume, the first week is lighter: up to 7 days paused → 80 %, up to 14 days → 70 %, longer → 60 % and back to the base phase. Workouts during the pause are removed.
pause.resumeInfo: If you resume today, your first week back is at {{percent}} % of your last full training week.
pause.resumeBase: If you resume today, your first week back is at {{percent}} % and the plan goes back to the base phase.
pause.resumeNoChange: The pause has not started yet – resuming simply cancels it.

week.title: This week is different
week.hint: Set the time you have on each day of this week. Days away get no training and no commute. Only this week is rebuilt – it keeps as much of its training load as the time allows.

travel.title: Travel mode
travel.entryHint: Train on the road: hotel-room strength and alternatives for rides and swims.
travel.hint: While you travel, strength switches to bodyweight and band exercises, runs are planned by time, and rides and swims get an easy alternative of similar load – as long as nothing else is available there. No commutes on travel days.
travel.bike: A bike or indoor trainer is available
travel.endBeforeStart: The last day must not be before the first.

commutes.title: Commutes
commutes.entryHint: Bike, run or walk to work – counted as easy training.
commutes.hint: Commutes are planned first as easy sessions and count towards your training load. On the day, you can skip one with a tap.

winter.title: Winter sports
winter.entryHint: Skiing, ski touring or snowshoeing as part of your plan.
winter.hint: In your winter period, easy and long sessions get a winter variant with the same training load. Key sessions for a race stay in your sport.

run.recovery: Very easy running helps your legs recover from the last hard session.
run.easy: Easy Zone 2 running builds your aerobic engine – the base of every plan.
run.easyStrides: An easy run with a few short, relaxed strides keeps your legs quick without tiring you.
run.long: The long run builds endurance and teaches your body to run efficiently for longer.
run.uphillHike: Steep hiking and running builds the climbing strength mountain events demand.
run.progression: Starting easy and finishing faster teaches pacing and builds fitness without a hard interval session.
run.fartlek: Playful surges by feel – a gentle introduction to faster running that works on any terrain.
run.hillsShort: Short hill sprints build power and running economy with low injury risk.
run.hillsLong: Longer hill repeats build strength endurance at threshold effort.
run.tempo: Threshold running raises the pace you can hold for a long time.
run.vo2: Intervals at VO2max pace raise your aerobic ceiling.
run.racePace: Running at goal race pace makes that pace feel familiar and controlled on race day.
run.downhill: Controlled descents prepare your legs for the eccentric load of downhill racing.
run.commute: Running to work counts as easy training – it is part of the plan.

bike.recovery: An easy spin with high cadence flushes your legs after hard days.
bike.endurance: Steady Zone 2 riding builds aerobic fitness with little fatigue.
bike.long: The long ride builds the endurance you need for long days in the saddle.
bike.commute: Your commute counts as easy training – it is part of the plan.
bike.tempo: Steady tempo efforts build muscular endurance.
bike.sweetspot: Sweet-spot intervals give a lot of fitness for the time invested.
bike.threshold: Threshold intervals raise the power you can sustain for an hour.
bike.vo2: Short, hard intervals raise your maximum aerobic power.
bike.climb: Climbing efforts build strength on the bike and prepare you for hilly routes.
bike.cadence: Cadence drills improve pedalling efficiency inside an easy ride.

swim.technique: Drills improve your stroke – in swimming, technique is the fastest way to get faster.
swim.aerobic: Steady aerobic swimming builds endurance in the water.
swim.easy: Easy continuous swimming keeps the feel for the water without extra fatigue.
swim.css: Repeats at your Critical Swim Speed raise the pace you can hold over distance.
swim.speed: Short fast repeats with long rest build speed and a strong stroke.
swim.openwater: Sighting and continuous swimming prepare you for open-water racing.

why.brick: Running straight off the bike teaches your legs the transition you will feel on race day.

winter.xcski: Cross-country skiing builds the same aerobic fitness – with less impact on your legs.
winter.xcskiIntervals: Intervals on skis train your threshold while giving your running legs a break.
winter.skitour: Ski touring builds climbing endurance; the ascent is the training.
winter.snowshoe: Snowshoeing is a low-impact, full-body endurance session.

benchmark.run5k: A 5 km time trial updates your pace zones and race prediction.
benchmark.run30: A 30-minute solo effort measures your threshold heart rate (average of the last 20 minutes).
benchmark.swimCss: A 400 m and 200 m time trial updates your Critical Swim Speed.
benchmark.bikeFtp: A 20-minute test estimates your FTP (about 95 % of the average power).

strength.peakrBase: General strength now makes you more robust for the harder endurance weeks ahead.
strength.peakrBuild: Heavy, low-rep strength and jumps make you more economical and powerful.
strength.peakrPeak: A short maintenance session keeps your strength while the endurance work peaks.
strength.coreMobility: Core and mobility work keeps you moving well without tiring your legs.
strength.fullBody: A full-body session from your split.
strength.upper: Upper-body work from your split – it does not tire your legs for running or riding.
strength.legs: Leg day from your split, placed so it does not hurt your key endurance sessions.
strength.runners: Runner-specific strength for hips, calves and single-leg stability.
strength.routine: Your own routine, placed so it fits around the endurance sessions.

walk.commute: Walking to work is gentle, low-impact movement – it counts a little towards your load.

notes.intensityBalance: Planned {{type}} session made easy to keep about 80 % of your training easy.
notes.loadCap: Shortened so this week does not increase the training load by more than 10 %.
notes.loadCapEasy: Planned {{type}} session made shorter and easy so this week does not increase the load by more than 10 %.
notes.recoveryWeek: Recovery week – less load so your body can absorb the training.
notes.taperWeek: Taper – less volume, some sharpness, fresh legs for race day.
notes.shortPreparation: Only {{weeks}} weeks until your race – {{recommended}} weeks are recommended, so the plan is compressed.
notes.strengthMerged: Not enough free days for your split: sessions are combined into {{sessions}}.
notes.strengthNoDay: No free day for strength this week.
notes.strengthSkipped: The {{type}} strength session did not fit this week without hurting a key session.
notes.noRaceDate: No race date yet – your plan runs the recommended {{weeks}} weeks. Add the date anytime and the plan adapts.
notes.eased: Made easier: the planned {{type}} session is now easy, so you do not have two hard days in a row.

disclaimer.title: Before you start
disclaimer.text: Peakr gives general training guidance and is not medical advice. If you have a heart condition, high blood pressure, are pregnant, take medication or have any other health concern, talk to your doctor before starting. Stop training and get help if you feel chest pain, dizziness or unusual shortness of breath.
disclaimer.confirm: I have read this and train at my own responsibility.

insights.title: Good to know
insights.zone2: Your Zone 2 is {{min}}–{{max}} bpm. Most of your training happens here – easy enough to talk, hard enough to build your engine.
insights.zone2Estimate: Your Zone 2 is about {{min}}–{{max}} bpm (estimated from your age). Most of your training happens here. You can refine it anytime in Profile → Training zones.

goal.triathlon: Triathlon plans start with roughly {{swim}} % swim, {{bike}} % bike and {{run}} % run – adjusted to your week.
goal.race: For this race at least {{weeks}} weeks of preparation are recommended. Your plan builds up in phases and tapers before race day.
goal.weightloss: Training supports weight loss best together with nutrition: easy sessions you can keep up, plus strength to keep muscle.
goal.fitness: Your plan loops build and recovery blocks, so you keep getting fitter without burning out.

run.threshold: Your threshold pace is about {{pace}} /km – the pace you could hold for about an hour. Your pace zones are based on it.
run.thresholdFromEasy: From your easy pace we estimate a threshold pace of about {{pace}} /km. A test run in the plan will make it precise.
run.noReference: No problem – your runs are guided by heart rate, and a short test run in the plan sets your pace zones.

swim.css: Your Critical Swim Speed is {{pace}} /100 m. Swim sets are prescribed relative to it.
swim.noTimes: Your swim sets start with standard paces; a CSS test in the plan makes them personal.
swim.technique: We start with technique and short intervals, so you can swim longer without a break soon.

insights.availability: You have {{days}} training days and up to {{hours}} hours per week. The plan uses less at the start and builds up gradually – never more than 10 % per week.

targetDate.ok: {{weeks}} weeks until race day – enough for a full build-up ({{recommended}} weeks recommended).
targetDate.short: Only {{weeks}} weeks until race day – {{recommended}} are recommended, so your plan is compressed. Getting to the start healthy comes first.
targetDate.none: No race date yet: your plan runs {{weeks}} weeks – the recommended preparation – and ends with a taper. Add the date later and the plan adapts.

barriers.time: Busy weeks happen: you can rebuild a single week in seconds and the plan keeps your training load.
barriers.motivation: Each session tells you why it matters, and you see your progress week by week.
barriers.injury: Your load grows at most 10 % per week, with a recovery week every 3–4 weeks and never two hard days in a row.
barriers.knowledge: Every session comes with clear targets – heart-rate zone, duration and structure.
barriers.rigid: Move sessions anytime: the week rebalances itself and warns you if two hard days end up back to back.
barriers.boredom: Your plan mixes sports, terrain and session types – and winter sports count too.
barriers.none: Great starting point. Let’s build a plan that keeps it that way.

insights.weightloss: A safe pace is at most {{kg}} kg per week (1 % of your body weight). Your training plan supports it; nutrition tracking comes with the Training + Nutrition plan.
insights.commute: Your commute adds about {{hours}} h of easy training on {{days}} days a week. It counts towards your plan, so the other sessions fit around it.
insights.winter: From December to March your plan offers winter variants of your easy and long sessions – with the same training load. You can change the winter period anytime.

workoutTypes.title: Workout types
workoutTypes.entryHint: What easy run, tempo, intervals & co. mean – and why they are in your plan.
workoutTypes.intro: Your calendar shows each session by its type. Tap a workout for the exact steps and targets; here you find what each type is for.

run.easy.name: Easy run
run.easy.description: Running at a pace where you can still hold a conversation – heart rate in Zone 2 (Zone 1 for recovery runs). Some easy runs end with strides: 15–20 seconds of relaxed, quick running.
run.easy.why: Builds your aerobic base, strengthens muscles and tendons and helps you recover. Most of your running should be easy.

run.long.name: Long run
run.long.short: Your longest run of the week, at an easy effort
run.long.description: A steady run clearly longer than your other runs, mostly in Zone 2. Go slower than you think – time on your feet counts, not pace.
run.long.why: Improves endurance and fat burning and gets body and mind ready for longer races.

run.tempo.name: Tempo run
run.tempo.description: After a warm-up you run one long block – or a few shorter ones – at threshold or race pace. Progression runs that get faster towards the end belong here too.
run.tempo.why: Raises the pace you can hold for a long time – the key for 10 km up to the marathon.

run.intervals.name: Intervals
run.intervals.description: Repeats of about 1–5 minutes at a hard effort – or a playful fartlek – with easy jogging in between, always with a proper warm-up and cool-down.
run.intervals.why: Improves your VO₂max, speed and running economy.

run.hills.name: Hills
run.hills.description: Short or long climbs run hard with easy recoveries on the way down – or steady hiking and running on steep terrain, plus downhill technique.
run.hills.why: Builds strength, power and running form with less impact than fast flat running, and prepares you for hilly races.

run.test.name: Test run
run.test.short: A benchmark that calibrates your zones
run.test.description: A time trial – e.g. 5 km or 30 minutes – at the best effort you can sustain. Your result updates your paces and zones.
run.test.why: Keeps your training targets right as you get fitter.

bike.easy.name: Easy ride
bike.easy.description: Steady riding in Zone 2 at a cadence that feels smooth. Recovery rides and bike commutes count as easy rides too.
bike.easy.why: Builds aerobic endurance with very little stress on your legs.

bike.long.name: Long ride
bike.long.short: Your longest ride of the week
bike.long.description: Hours in the saddle at an easy, steady effort. A good time to practise eating and drinking on the bike.
bike.long.why: Builds endurance for long events like a gran fondo or a triathlon.

bike.tempo.name: Tempo ride
bike.tempo.description: Longer blocks at an effort that needs focus but stays under control.
bike.tempo.why: Raises the power you can sustain on long rides.

bike.threshold.name: Threshold ride
bike.threshold.description: Blocks of about 8–20 minutes just below or at your threshold (FTP) with short recoveries.
bike.threshold.why: The most time-efficient way to lift your FTP.

bike.intervals.name: Intervals
bike.intervals.short: Hard efforts of a few minutes
bike.intervals.description: Repeats of about 2–5 minutes well above threshold with equally long recoveries.
bike.intervals.why: Improves your VO₂max and your ability to handle surges and short climbs.

bike.hills.name: Climbing ride
bike.hills.description: Seated and standing efforts on climbs – or high resistance on the indoor trainer.
bike.hills.why: Builds climbing strength and teaches you to pace long ascents.

bike.technique.name: Cadence drills
bike.technique.description: Easy riding with blocks of high and low cadence.
bike.technique.why: Makes your pedalling more efficient and coordinated.

bike.test.name: FTP test
bike.test.short: A benchmark for your power zones
bike.test.description: A 20-minute all-out effort after a thorough warm-up; about 95 % of the average power is your FTP.
bike.test.why: Keeps your power and heart-rate targets right.

swim.technique.name: Technique swim
swim.technique.description: Short repeats with drills for catch, kick and body position, with plenty of rest.
swim.technique.why: Better technique makes you faster with less effort – the biggest lever in swimming.

swim.easy.name: Easy swim
swim.easy.description: Steady swimming at a comfortable pace, a little slower than your CSS pace.
swim.easy.why: Builds swim endurance and feel for the water.

swim.threshold.name: CSS swim
swim.threshold.description: Repeats of 100–400 m at your Critical Swim Speed with short rests.
swim.threshold.why: Raises the pace you can hold over longer distances.

swim.speed.name: Speed swim
swim.speed.description: Sprints of 25–50 m with long rests.
swim.speed.why: Improves top speed and the power of your stroke.

swim.openwater.name: Open-water swim
swim.openwater.short: Practice for lakes and the sea
swim.openwater.description: Continuous swimming with sighting, swimming in a group and changes of pace.
swim.openwater.why: Prepares you for race conditions without lane lines and walls.

swim.test.name: CSS test
swim.test.short: A benchmark for your swim paces
swim.test.description: A 400 m and a 200 m time trial; together they give your Critical Swim Speed.
swim.test.why: Sets the paces of every swim session.

brick.brick.name: Brick
brick.brick.description: A ride followed immediately by a run, just like in a triathlon or duathlon.
brick.brick.why: Teaches your legs to run well after cycling.

strength.strength.name: Strength
strength.strength.short: Strength training that fits your plan
strength.strength.description: Your strength session – the Peakr programme, your own split or your own routine. The workout lists every exercise with sets, reps and rest.
strength.strength.why: Makes you more robust, prevents injuries and improves running economy. Heavy leg sessions are never placed right before a key session.

winter.easy.name: Winter endurance
winter.easy.description: Easy endurance on snow that replaces a run or ride with the same training load.
winter.easy.why: Real training in winter – full body and low impact.

winter.intervals.name: Ski intervals
winter.intervals.description: Repeats at a hard effort on cross-country skis.
winter.intervals.why: A strong aerobic stimulus that uses the whole body.

commute.commute.name: Commute
commute.commute.short: Getting to work by bike, running or on foot
commute.commute.description: Your regular trip to work or school, one way or there and back. Ridden, run or walked at an easy effort – no pace to hit.
commute.commute.why: Easy minutes that build your aerobic base without extra time. They count towards your training load, so the rest of the week is planned around them.

hr.title: Heart rate zones

methodInfo.percentMax: Zones as a percentage of your maximum heart rate. Simple and a good start.
methodInfo.karvonen: Uses your heart rate reserve (max minus resting). More personal, because it reflects your fitness.
methodInfo.lthr: Zones from your lactate threshold heart rate (Joe Friel). The most precise if you know your threshold.

hr.autoMethod: Chosen automatically: Karvonen as soon as you enter your resting heart rate.
hr.hrMaxEstimateNote: Estimated from your age (208 − 0.7 × age). A measured value makes your zones more accurate.

run.intro: Enter a recent race or all-out time trial. The more recent, the better.
run.thresholdNote: About the pace you could hold for one hour.
run.empty: Add a recent race result to get running pace zones.

indoorNotes.treadmillSplit: Long runs on the treadmill get monotonous – two halves with a short break in between are fine, the load stays the same.
indoorNotes.treadmillNoDescent: Treadmills can't go downhill, so the descents of this session are missing. If the downhill part matters, move it to a dry day instead.
indoorNotes.trainerFan: No airflow indoors: use a fan and keep a bottle in reach – your heart rate rises faster on the trainer.
indoorNotes.trainerCapped: {{indoor}} min instead of {{outdoor}} min: without coasting, trainer minutes count more. If the full ride matters, move it to another day.
indoorNotes.poolOpenWater: No sighting in the pool – lift your head every 6–8 strokes on a few lengths to keep practising it.

spo2_avg.label: Blood oxygen (SpO2)
spo2_avg.about: Average SpO2 reading of the day where your watch measured it.

respiration_avg.label: Respiration
respiration_avg.about: Average breaths per minute while awake.

weight.label: Weight
weight.about: From your connected scale or your own entries in the source app.

vo2max.label: VO2max (estimate)
vo2max.about: Your watch's VO2max estimate in ml/kg/min.

body_battery_high.label: Body Battery high (Garmin)
body_battery_high.about: Highest Body Battery value of the day, exactly as Garmin reports it.

body_battery_low.label: Body Battery low (Garmin)
body_battery_low.about: Lowest Body Battery value of the day, exactly as Garmin reports it.

sleep.title: Sleep
sleep.reads: Sleep duration, sleep stages, bed and wake time, Garmin sleep score

stress.title: Stress and Body Battery
stress.reads: Garmin stress level, Body Battery high and low

activity.title: Daily activity
activity.reads: Steps, floors, intensity minutes, active calories, VO2max estimate

body_comp.title: Body composition
body_comp.reads: Weight, body fat, muscle mass, BMI from a connected scale

womens_health.title: Women's health
womens_health.reads: Cycle tracking data. Off unless you switch it on. Peakr does not show it yet; switching it on only allows reading it once that view exists.

overview.title: Health
overview.historyFromConnection: Data starts on the day you connected – this Garmin connection does not deliver older days.
overview.backfilling: Fetching your older data – this can take a while.
overview.syncError: The last fetch did not work. Peakr tries again on its own.
overview.pushHint: New values arrive by themselves after your watch syncs with Garmin Connect.

baseline.building: Your usual range appears after {{needed}} days with data ({{count}} so far)
baseline.trendFlat: About the same as the 30 days before
baseline.ownHistory: Compared with your own history only – never with other people.

missing.not_connected: Connect Garmin or Health Connect to see this.
missing.not_enabled: Not switched on. Turn on "{{group}}" in Health data settings.
missing.not_provided: Your connected sources do not provide this.
missing.no_data: Nothing recorded in the last 7 days. Your watch records this only while you wear it (sleep and HRV overnight) and after it has synced.

empty.title: Your body data in Peakr
empty.body: Connect Garmin to see sleep, HRV, resting heart rate, stress and more next to your training – compared with your own history.

detail.chartA11y: Line chart of {{metric}} over {{period}}: {{count}} values, latest {{latest}}.
detail.hardSessionsHint: Dips and rises often follow hard training. Each dot under the chart is one of these sessions.
detail.noHardSessions: No hard sessions in this period.
detail.consult: If this keeps up, talk to a doctor.

sleep.noStages: No sleep stages for this night.

body.title: Body composition
body.none: No scale measurements yet. Weigh in on a connected scale to see them here.

consent.title: Health data
consent.intro: Choose what Peakr may read. Each group is separate, you can switch it off at any time, and switching a group off deletes what Peakr stored for it.
consent.privacy: Your health data is stored encrypted, is never shown to anyone else and is never used to train models.
consent.saveError: Could not save. Check your connection and try again.
consent.garminComing: Garmin health data arrives once Garmin has approved Peakr.
consent.deviceBody: Reads the same groups from Health Connect on this phone (the last 30 days). The values stay on this phone. Garmin values win when both have one for the same day.
consent.deleteBody: Deletes every health value Peakr stored, on the server and on this phone. Your account, plan and connections stay.

developer.title: Developer: Garmin personal API key
developer.body: For your own account only. Garmin's Personal API is meant for a person's own tools, so this stays a developer option. The key is sent to Peakr's server once, stored encrypted and never kept on this phone.
developer.connectedKey: Connected with a personal API key

errors.invalid_key: Garmin did not accept this key.
errors.already_connected: Garmin is already connected with OAuth.
errors.unavailable: Garmin could not be reached. Try again later.

recovery.confirmBody: Peakr eases today's session (shorter, lower intensity). You can change it back in the plan.
recovery.consult: If this keeps up, talk to a doctor.

preview.title: Part of your subscription
preview.body: Your forecast and week 1 are free. The full plan – editing, routes, integrations, exports and your health data – starts with the 7-day free trial.

readOnly.title: Your plan is read-only
readOnly.body: Your subscription has ended. Your plan and history stay here; changes, routes, integrations and exports need an active subscription.
